html:
The Chiapanecs were a people of the central valley of Chiapas in southern Mexico, around the Grijalva River and the town of Chiapa de Corzo. The state of Chiapas takes its name from them. They spoke an Oto-Manguean language, related to languages far to the north, which suggests they had migrated south some centuries before the Spanish came.

They were feared warriors, kept their independence from the Aztecs and dominated neighbours such as the Zoque. Spanish forces conquered them in the 1520s; a later legend says many leapt into the Sumidero Canyon rather than surrender. Under New Spain they slowly lost their language, which died out in the 1900s.
